definition: Working Memory Index is an index score from the Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale that represents working memory as part of a person’s overall cognitive profile. It can be used to compare relative strengths and weaknesses in cognitive functioning across individuals or groups.

reasons: The packet does not define “Working Memory Index” as an index that “represents working memory as part of a person’s overall cognitive profile.” It only states that the study compared “Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale index scores” including the Working Memory Index.

The packet does not support the claim that the Working Memory Index “can be used to compare relative strengths and weaknesses in cognitive functioning across individuals or groups.” The text only reports group comparisons in this specific study context (ASD vs ADHD men) without establishing a general use statement.
